title: Rapid response regression: multiplex prioritization causing initial-response slowdowns across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Avery Martinez
description:
Summary:
A regression rolled out as part of a multiplex prioritization heuristic (runtime change: prioritize large-batch throughput by slightly deferring small single-request work) caused a measurable increase in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and drop in tokens/sec for short, low-token requests across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Impact shows up most strongly for single-turn chat completions and low-prefix generation for smaller models and non-cached KV contexts.

Impact observed:
- 25-60% increase in median TTFT for requests <128 tokens on impacted hosts.
- Overall tokens/sec down ~18% on multiplexed clusters during regional bursts.
- Multiple escalations from customers (notably Acme Health and Ember Analytics) reporting slow initial responses and degraded UX for chat endpoints.
- A few Dedicated customers reported SLA breaches for p50 TTFT on pinned pools.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1. Send 50k single-turn small requests (avg 32 tokens) to hosted endpoint under steady background multiplexed workload.
2. Compare first-byte latency distribution on runtime-1.22 vs runtime-1.21.
3. Observe disproportionate queuing of small requests behind larger batches when prioritization scoring applied.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- 2026-02-28 03:40 UTC: Toggle feature flag multiplex-priority-v2 -> off for Hosted region us-west-2 (rolled back change).
- 2026-02-28 04:12 UTC: Applied emergency affinity override on a subset of Dedicated pools to ensure small requests are fast-tracked.
- In Private: provided customers instructions to pin runtime to 1.21 and a migration guard doc.

Hypothesis / Root cause:
The prioritization heuristic weighted expected throughput improvement over first-byte latency, using a score that favored larger batches with KV warm rates assumed to be high. That scoring function failed to account for workload skew and the presence of many small, cache-miss requests for certain models. As a result, small requests were deprioritized and queued behind larger batching windows, increasing TTFT and reducing observed tokens/sec.

Proposed permanent fix (plan):
1) Rework prioritization score to include an explicit first-byte latency penalty for single-request flows and models with low KV hit-rate.
2) Add adaptive short-window fast-track path: requests under 128 tokens or flagged as low-latency-critical bypass batching up to a configurable token/time threshold.
3) Improve telemetry: emit per-request priority score and queue-delay metrics, and add alerting for p50 TTFT regressions per pool/model.
4) Add e2e integration tests that simulate skewed small-request workloads in CI for prioritization heuristics.

Rollback/Hotpatch decision:
Given customer impact and SLA risk, we executed a full rollback for Hosted and coordinated targeted overrides for Dedicated. For Private customers we recommended downgrades and provided a hotpatch script to revert the prioritization scoring in local deployments. The permanent fix work is prioritized as P0 for the next two cycles and split into incremental deliverables so we can deploy safe improvements quickly.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- p50 TTFT for small requests (<128 tokens) returns to baseline + <10% of pre-regression numbers across Hosted/Dedicated/Private in production tests.
- tokens/sec under representative mixed workload recovers to within 5% of previous steady-state.
- New telemetry emits request_priority, queue_duration, kv_hit_rate for each multiplexed request.
- No regression in large-batch throughput beyond 3% from baseline after changes.

Notes for QA and SRE:
- Watch consoles: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime/priority-heuristic and the per-customer TTFT view.
- Incident runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PRIORITY-HEURISTIC-INCIDENT.
- Tagged smoke tests added to Canary: canary/priority-heuristic-small-request-suite.
